exact_reviewed_rows.text: In the Government of Odisha’s account, cloth receives a coating of chalk and tamarind-seed glue before painting. Borders come first, then a brush sketch, flat colours and fine black outlines. Krishna and Jagannath are among the subjects. The smooth prepared surface and the successive marks are different parts of making the picture; this account does not establish the materials of every work today.

Joanna Williams describes large cloth paintings with narrative scenes around their edges. Her 1996 study also shows how painting was learned: pupils practised, filled images drawn by a teacher and worked on borders. A large picture could involve several hands. These are documented working relationships, not evidence that skill is inherited or that every painter belongs to the Chitrakara community.
